subject: Urgent: Compatibility hotpatch applied to model-serving nodes
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@nimbushealth.com>, ops@nimbushealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Urgent: Compatibility hotpatch applied to model-serving nodes

Alex — quick heads up,

We detected a compatibility mismatch between a recent upstream CUDA driver rollout in Nimbus Health's cloud region and our model-serving binaries that began manifesting as intermittent 503s for short sequences (primarily < 128 tokens) around 08:40 PDT. Our engineering team validated a targeted hotpatch (compatibility shim + kernel selection tweak) and performed a coordinated rolling restart of the affected node pool at 08:58 PDT.

Impact summary:
- Window: ~08:40–09:00 PDT
- Symptom: intermittent 503/connection-reset for short requests, increased tail latency for generation routes
- Scope: a subset of serving pods in us-west-2 (your routed traffic); estimated ~0.8% of requests during the window

What we did:
- Applied hotfix v1.0.3 to model-serving runtime (no model artifacts changed)
- Performed staged rolling restarts with canary validation between pods
- Enabled additional monitoring and extended tracing for 24h

Why this happened: an automated driver upgrade in the region exposed a kernel incompatibility with our optimized attention path; the hotpatch provides a safe fallback kernel selection while we validate a long-term binary rebuild.

Attachments: hotfix-compatibility-1.0.3-notes.pdf (release notes) and kube-rolling-log.txt (rolling restart trace).

Immediate ask: please validate that your critical integration flows are back to normal and share any anomalous traces you still observe. We will follow up with a short postmortem and next steps by EOD tomorrow.

Sorry for the disruption — I know timing is bad. Im standing by for any questions.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0147
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@nimbushealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@nimbushealth.com
Date: 2026-05-10T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: Compatibility hotpatch applied to model-serving nodes

Thanks Rishi — appreciate the quick action.

We saw the 503s during the 08:45–08:55 window on our side; luckily retries handled most flows but a handful of queued jobs did fail and required manual requeue. I sent a short dump to ops@nimbushealth.com earlier.

Two questions:
1) Do you expect any degradation from the shim compared to the long-term fix? Latency-sensitive endpoints (clinical-assist) are sensitive to extra tail latency.
2) Can you confirm whether any logs containing PHI traversed the extended tracing hooks you enabled? We need to log that for compliance.

- Alex
Alex Mercer
Head of Integrations, Nimbus Health
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neil Ops <ops@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-10T11:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: Compatibility hotpatch applied to model-serving nodes

Internal note / response to Alex:

1) Short answer: the shim may add ~2–6ms at the 99th pct on very short sequences; for most production flows this is within our SLOs but well quantify and share a precise delta by EOD.
2) Tracing change rationale: we temporarily increased metadata sampling for the affected request paths; we did NOT enable payload capture or full request bodies. No PHI bodies were collected. We logged request ids, routing metadata, and kernel selection details only.

Im attaching the rolling restart kube logs (kube-rolling-log.txt) and the hotfix release notes. Were scheduling a rebuild of the optimized attention binary; plan is to release a durable fix in the next maintenance window if validation goes well.

David
David Kim
Staff Software Engineer, Runtime
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@nimbushealth.com>, ops@nimbushealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-11T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Post-event summary and next steps for 2026-05-10 hotpatch

Alex —

Thanks again for the quick confirmation and for flagging the few manual requeues. As promised, short post-event summary:

Timeline (PDT):
- 08:40 — first automated alerts for elevated 5xx on generation routes
- 08:46 — root-cause (driver/kernel mismatch) identified by runtime team
- 08:58 — hotfix v1.0.3 applied and rolling restarts initiated
- 09:00 — traffic stabilized; error rate returned to baseline

Impact: ~0.8% of requests affected in your routed pool; median latency unaffected, 99th pct increased by ~3–5ms for short sequences during the fallback path. No persisted data loss.

Compliance note: tracing did not capture request bodies or PHI. We retained request ids for tracing and have exported relevant logs to a secure bucket as part of evidence (link below).

Action items:
- Redwood: continue validation of binary rebuild (David) — target: next maintenance window (2026-05-17) for permanent rollout.
- Redwood: share quantified latency delta and test harness results by 2026-05-12 EOD (David).
- Nimbus: share any failed job ids that need manual reconciliation; Redwood will assist.

Links and artifacts:
- Status/Incident: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-05-10-compat-hotpatch
- Jira: JIRA-RED-9217
- Artifacts (secure): https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/NimbusHealth-postmortem
- Attachments: hotfix-compatibility-1.0.3-notes.pdf, kube-rolling-log.txt

If youd like we can schedule a 20-minute sync to walk through the rebuild plan and any additional mitigations.

Regards,
Rishi
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
